question_stem: A public good is generally characterised by
option_A: rivalry in consumption and easy exclusion of non-payers
option_B: non-rivalry in consumption and difficulty excluding non-payers
option_D: consumption by one person preventing all others from using it
answer_explanation: A pure public good is generally non-rival in consumption and non-excludable: one person's use does not substantially reduce availability to others, and it is difficult to prevent people from benefiting.

question_stem: A group of cement manufacturers establishes several plants in the same area near limestone deposits and major transport routes. This concentration of similar industries in one area is best described as:
answer_explanation: Localization of industry occurs when firms in the same or closely related industries concentrate in a particular geographical area. Such concentration may be encouraged by access to raw materials, transport, skilled labour, suppliers and supporting infrastructure.

question_stem: In the short run, a firm operating under monopolistic competition may earn supernormal profit when, at its profit-maximising output, the price it charges
option_A: is greater than its average total cost
option_B: is lower than its average total cost
option_C: is exactly equal to its average total cost
option_D: is unrelated to its average total cost
answer_explanation: A firm earns supernormal (abnormal) profit when total revenue exceeds total cost. At the chosen output, this is represented by price (average revenue) being above average total cost. Equality represents normal profit, while price below average total cost indicates a loss.
